solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Macabre kill unravelled — he threatens to expose offender

indicators.note: something unravelled is pulled apart and comes out in a different arrangement, so these two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A grisly murder is solved, and someone threatens to expose the killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelled' rearranges the eleven letters of MACABRE KILL.
explanation.definitionFit: An extortioner demands money by threatening to reveal a wrongdoer's secrets.

clue.text: Succession followed by monarch such as Queen Mary

parts.note: a line is a succession, as in a line of kings
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Royal succession passes to a monarch like Queen Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Mary was a famous Cunard ocean liner, not the queen herself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cunard ship of that name was an ocean-going passenger vessel.

clue.text: They'll make champs toast including women

indicators.note: including means containing, so the drinking toast takes in the letter for women

parts.note: cheers is a toast when raising glasses

explanation.surface: Raising glasses to the winners, the ladies join in the toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champs' looks like winners but is the verb champ, to chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch noisily, so those who chomp are the ones producing it.

clue.text: Provide with engine needing short time to get up

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief time
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Installing a motor needs a moment before it gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit a vehicle with an engine is to make it motor-powered.

clue.text: Totter up gets sly look

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to reel is to stagger or totter

explanation.surface: Someone staggering upright gets a crafty glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a suggestive or knowing sidelong glance.

clue.text: Desiring changes, this gives a good view

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters of desiring are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wanting change seeks a vantage point.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat right beside a boxing ring offers spectators the closest view.

clue.text: Platform setting out team's info

indicators.note: setting out suggests laying things out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive here supplies its S as a letter

explanation.surface: A document lays out the team's information.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's platform is its set of declared policies, the same as its published programme.

clue.text: Spy on headquarters, providing interference

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted within an organisation
a station is a base or headquarters, as in a police station

explanation.surface: A spy at head office is meddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted interference with someone, harassment or abuse, is the sense here.

clue.text: I am a success in perfect form

parts.note: contracted to I'm, written without the apostrophe
a go can mean a success, as in 'make a go of it'

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being a hit while looking flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: An imago is the final, fully developed adult stage of an insect, hence its 'perfect form'.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomologists call the mature adult insect stage the perfect or final form.

clue.text: Working contract for stylish gnashers?

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
gnashers is British slang for teeth, so a set of false ones

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what agreement covers a fancy set of false teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: GNASHERS is jokey British slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal agreement binding an apprentice to work for a master.

clue.text: Musical style of Rice perhaps in vogue

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, the lyricist's name placed within the fashion word

parts.note: a rage is a craze or fashion, as in 'all the rage'
Tim Rice, lyricist of Evita, is one example of a Rice

explanation.surface: A remark on which genre of music the lyricist Rice favours being fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Rice is the British lyricist who worked with Andrew Lloyd Webber; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of a Rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano genre popular around 1900.

clue.text: Rainforest inhabitant got back round bank, right

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the other pieces, enclosing them
back tells us to read the word got from right to left

parts.note: a reef is a ridge or bank of rock or sand near the water's surface

explanation.surface: A creature of the jungle returns around a riverbank to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: This small arboreal amphibian lives in tropical forests, so it is a typical jungle dweller.

clue.text: It shifts cargo from errant ports at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A vessel moves goods away from wayward harbours across the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that carries freight, such as a car transporter, moves goods.

clue.text: Illustration showing mostly favourable quality about Greek character

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened virtue word surrounds the letter
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: grace is a pleasing or favourable quality
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A picture shows a mostly admirable trait in a Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts GRACE to GRAC, which goes 'about' PHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphic is a picture or diagram used to illustrate text.

clue.text: Regular performer let round team

indicators.note: round says the hire word encloses the team word

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A landlord lets a property to a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident performer is one engaged to play regularly at a venue, such as a house band.

clue.text: A politician's sound equipment

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A member of parliament owns a hi-fi rig.
explanation.definitionFit: Amplifiers boost signals for loudspeakers and are standard audio gear.

clue.text: Heartless clique upset a politician producing intense discomfort

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top
heartless means losing the centre, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: a group is a clique or set
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A cruel faction overturns a politician, causing great distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' cuts GROUP to GRUP, which 'upset' turns into PURG.
explanation.definitionFit: The theological place of suffering before heaven is used figuratively for torment.

clue.text: Indication to look elsewhere in document for leak

definitions.text: Indication to look elsewhere in document
definitions.meaning: a cross-reference instruction, telling the reader to turn to another page
a slow escape of liquid through a gap

explanation.definitionFit: Water oozing through a crack is a slow escape of liquid; a cross-reference sends readers to another page.

clue.text: Submitted before the Spanish guard

parts.note: sent in means submitted, as an entry
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An application was lodged before the Spanish security officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry or lookout keeps watch, so is a guard.

clue.text: Weapon gathered aluminium alloy

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
met means came together or gathered
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A firearm is assembled from light metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze of copper and tin used formerly for cannon is a kind of alloy.

clue.text: Native-American dance leading to onset of inundation

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance party

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the first letter of inundation is used

explanation.surface: A tribal dance is performed just before a flood begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Pueblo people of north-eastern Arizona.

clue.text: Ghastly house I'd renovated

indicators.note: renovated means rebuilt, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: An estate agent admits the place they have done up is hideous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something frightful or very ugly.

clue.text: One lacking belief in Italy's foremost composer

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen, someone without mainstream religious belief

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so the first letter of Italy's

explanation.surface: An unbeliever in Italy becomes its leading composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Niccolò Paganini was the Italian violin virtuoso and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genoese violinist wrote the famous Caprices for solo violin, making him a noted composer.

clue.text: Entertainer to fool around TV etc

indicators.note: around says the trickery word wraps the broadcasting word

parts.note: to con someone is to fool them
television, radio and the press are collectively the media

explanation.surface: A performer is mocking television and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comic entertains audiences with jokes.

clue.text: Priest beheaded for serious crime

indicators.note: beheaded means the head or first letter is removed

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman executed for a grave offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a grave criminal offence.

clue.text: Keeps checks restricting irregular soldiers

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the restraint word holds the soldiers inside

parts.note: reins restrain or check, as one reins in a horse
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone holds back reins to control a band of part-time troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve, hence 'irregular soldiers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct synonym: to keep something is to continue to possess it.

clue.text: Drive bowling of Swann?

definitions.meaning: Graeme Swann was an England off-... bowler, so his style of bowling

explanation.walkthrough: Graeme Swann is a former England cricketer who bowled off-spin; the question mark flags him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure trip in a car and a cricket bowling technique share this word.

clue.text: Penny has to be keen about old apartment

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the eagerness word wraps the letter for old

parts.note: to enthuse is to show keenness

explanation.surface: Penny must show enthusiasm for a vintage flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A luxury flat on the top floor of a building is a well-known kind of apartment.

clue.text: High position — Jane holds one

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the heroine's surname takes the numeral inside

parts.note: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Brontë's heroine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Jane, the Brontë heroine, has one lofty place.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest is built on a crag or tall tree, a lofty vantage point.

clue.text: Assassinated President — heinous act — needs initially lots of lawyers

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was the US President shot in 1865
a sin is a wicked or heinous act

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of needs

explanation.surface: The killing of a President was a terrible deed that drew in many attorneys.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of London's four Inns of Court, professional bodies for barristers.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inn of Court is a society housing and admitting many barristers, so a body of lawyers.
